title: Understanding Zero-One Loss
text: Zero-one loss is a type of loss function used in classification problems. It counts the number of incorrect predictions made by the model. Unlike cross-entropy loss, which is differentiable and depends only on the model parameters (beta), zero-one loss also depends on the threshold (T) used for classification.

title: Role of Threshold in Zero-One Loss
text: In zero-one loss, the threshold T plays a crucial role because it determines the point at which the predicted probability is converted into a class label. This means that both beta and T are involved in minimizing the zero-one loss.

hintAnswer: Yes adjusting T changes the classification outcome affecting the zero-one loss.
title: Analyzing the Dependency
text: Consider how the threshold T affects the classification outcome. If T is adjusted, does it change the number of correct or incorrect predictions?

hintAnswer: Zero-one loss is affected by changes in T while cross-entropy loss is not.
title: Comparing Loss Functions
text: Compare how cross-entropy loss and zero-one loss depend on the parameters beta and T. Which one is affected by changes in T?

title: Conclusion on Parameters
text: Since zero-one loss depends on both beta and T, the parameters that minimize this loss, $$\beta_{ZO}$$ and $$T_{ZO}$$, are influenced by both. This makes the statement about them being only dependent on beta false.
